RNA Folding Notebook¶

This notebook generates RNA secondary structure predictions using ViennaRNA and visualizes them with forgi.

  • load precomputed SHAPE reactivity data,
  • sample sequences per experiment,
  • compute unconstrained and SHAPE-constrained folds,
  • and render comparison plots (SHAPE-colored bases).

The goal is to provide a compact, reproducible workflow for examining RNA folding behavior and assessing how reactivity values influence folding predictions.

Environment & Imports¶

This section sets up all required packages for RNA folding, data handling, and visualization.

SHAPE Reactivity Preprocessing¶

This section prepares the dataset for folding by:

  • detecting key columns (sequence, experiment labels, sequence IDs),
  • identifying all reactivity_* columns,
  • converting each row into a SHAPE vector aligned to its sequence,
  • grouping data by experiment type,
  • and writing the processed results to a compressed Parquet file.

The batching and vector conversion keep memory usage efficient when handling large RNA datasets.

In [4]:
# ================== CONFIG ==================
BATCH_ROWS = 2000                # tune for RAM / speed
FILL = np.float32(-999.0)        # ViennaRNA-style missing marker

# ================== COLUMN DETECTION ==================
# Required: sequence column
if "sequence" in train.columns:
    seq_col = "sequence"
else:
    raise ValueError("No 'sequence' column found in train.")

# Optional: experiment column
exp_col = None
for c in ("experiment_type", "exp", "experiment"):
    if c in train.columns:
        exp_col = c
        break

if exp_col is not None and not isinstance(train[exp_col].dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype):
    train[exp_col] = train[exp_col].astype("category")

# Optional: sequence_id column
seq_id_col = None
for c in ("sequence_id", "id", "seq_id"):
    if c in train.columns:
        seq_id_col = c
        break

# ================== REACTIVITY COLUMNS ==================
pat = re.compile(r"reactivity_(\d+)$")
keyed = []
for c in train.columns:
    m = pat.match(str(c))
    if m:
        keyed.append((int(m.group(1)), c))

react_cols = [c for _, c in sorted(keyed)]
if not react_cols:
    raise ValueError("No reactivity_* columns found in train.")

# ================== EXPERIMENT GROUPING ==================
def map_exp(x):
    if x == "DMS_MaP":
        return "DMS"
    if x == "2A3_MaP":
        return "2A3"
    return "ALL"

if exp_col is None:
    groups = [("ALL", train)]
else:
    groups = []
    cats = train[exp_col].cat.categories if hasattr(train[exp_col], "cat") else train[exp_col].unique()
    for lbl in cats:
        sub = train.loc[train[exp_col].astype(str).eq(str(lbl))]
        if len(sub):
            groups.append((map_exp(lbl), sub))

# ================== SEQUENCE → SHAPE VECTOR ==================
def row_to_shape(seq: str, row_vals: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    seq: RNA sequence (string)
    row_vals: reactivity values for this row (1-based positions in columns)
    Returns: float16 vector of length len(seq), filled with FILL where missing.
    """
    L = len(seq) if isinstance(seq, str) else 0
    if L <= 0:
        return np.full(0, FILL, dtype=np.float16)

    v = np.full(L, FILL, dtype=np.float16)

    vals = row_vals.astype(np.float32, copy=False)
    vals = vals[:L]  # truncate if we have more columns than sequence length

    mask = np.isfinite(vals)
    if mask.any():
        v[np.nonzero(mask)[0]] = vals[mask].astype(np.float16, copy=False)
    return v

# ================== CLEAN START: REMOVE OLD FILE ==================
if SAVE_PATH.exists():
    SAVE_PATH.unlink()

SAVE_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# ================== PARQUET WRITER LOOP ==================
writer = None
total_rows = 0

cols_needed = []
if seq_id_col:
    cols_needed.append(seq_id_col)
cols_needed.append(seq_col)
cols_needed.extend(react_cols)
cols_needed = [c for c in cols_needed if c is not None]

for exp_short, df_exp in groups:
    if df_exp.empty:
        continue

    df_exp = df_exp[cols_needed].copy()
    exp_rows = 0

    for start in range(0, len(df_exp), BATCH_ROWS):
        end = min(start + BATCH_ROWS, len(df_exp))
        batch = df_exp.iloc[start:end]

        # reactivity matrix
        R = batch[react_cols].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32, copy=False)

        out_rows = []
        seq_vals = batch[seq_col].astype("string").to_numpy()
        ids = batch[seq_id_col].to_numpy() if seq_id_col else None

        for i, seq in enumerate(seq_vals):
            seq_str = "" if seq is pd.NA else str(seq)
            vec = row_to_shape(seq_str, R[i])

            row = {
                "experiment": exp_short,
                "sequence": seq_str,
                "shape_vec": vec,
            }
            if ids is not None:
                row["sequence_id"] = ids[i]
            out_rows.append(row)

        df_out = pd.DataFrame(out_rows)

        # nice column order
        col_order = []
        if "sequence_id" in df_out.columns:
            col_order.append("sequence_id")
        col_order += ["sequence", "experiment", "shape_vec"]
        df_out = df_out[col_order]

        # convert ndarray → list for parquet
        df2 = df_out.copy()
        df2["shape_vec"] = df2["shape_vec"].apply(lambda a: a.tolist())

        table = pa.Table.from_pandas(df2, preserve_index=False)

        # lazily create writer when we see first chunk
        if writer is None:
            writer = pq.ParquetWriter(
                SAVE_PATH,
                table.schema,
                compression="zstd"
            )

        writer.write_table(table)
        batch_n = len(df_out)
        total_rows += batch_n
        exp_rows += batch_n

    # one summary line per experiment
    print(f"Experiment {exp_short}: wrote {exp_rows} rows")

if writer is not None:
    writer.close()

print(f"\nSaved fold_inputs to: {SAVE_PATH} with {total_rows} total rows")

SHAPE Handling & Folding Utilities¶

This section defines two core helpers:

  • to_float_list
    Cleans and normalizes SHAPE vectors by converting values to floats and replacing invalid entries with -999.0, the placeholder used by ViennaRNA for missing constraints.

  • fold_with_vienna
    Applies the Deigan SHAPE model to compute an MFE secondary structure using ViennaRNA, with automatic sequence normalization and constraint validation.

The shape_vec column is also forced to stay as Python lists to ensure compatibility with the folding functions.

In [12]:
def to_float_list(vec):
    """
    Convert a SHAPE reactivity vector (list/array) into a clean Python list[float].

    Rules:
      • Cast numeric values to float
      • Replace invalid / None / NaN / non-numeric values with -999.0
        (ViennaRNA uses -999 to indicate "missing constraint")
      • Always return a flat Python list, never NumPy array
    """
    # Ensure 1-D vector input: flatten numpy array or convert to 1-D array of objects
    if isinstance(vec, np.ndarray):
        v = vec.ravel()
    else:  # handle Python lists / pandas cells that may contain objects
        v = np.array(vec, dtype=object).ravel()

    out = []
    for x in v:
        # Missing values → placeholder
        if x is None:
            out.append(-999.0)
            continue

        # Try converting to float safely
        try:
            xf = float(x)
            # NaN / ±inf → missing
            out.append(xf if np.isfinite(xf) else -999.0)
        except Exception:
            # Non-numeric string / corrupted entry → missing
            out.append(-999.0)

    return out


def fold_with_vienna(seq, vec, m=1.9, b=-0.7):
    """
    Fold an RNA sequence using ViennaRNA with SHAPE constraints (Deigan model).

    Args:
        seq : RNA/DNA string (DNA 'T' automatically converted to RNA 'U')
        vec : SHAPE vector (raw input → cleaned with to_float_list)
        m, b: Deigan SHAPE parameters
              m = slope, b = intercept (default recommended values)

    Steps:
      • Convert sequence to RNA alphabet
      • Clean SHAPE values (replace invalid with -999)
      • Validate length match between sequence and SHAPE vector
      • Apply SHAPE constraints to ViennaRNA fold_compound
      • Compute MFE structure & energy

    Returns:
        ss  : predicted secondary structure (dot-bracket)
        mfe : minimum free energy (float)
    """
    # Convert DNA sequences to RNA form
    seq = str(seq).replace("T", "U")

    # Normalize SHAPE vector to float list with -999 for missing
    v = to_float_list(vec)

    # Sequence + SHAPE vector must match length
    if len(v) != len(seq):
        raise ValueError(f"shape_vec length {len(v)} != sequence length {len(seq)}")

    # Create ViennaRNA folding object
    fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq)

    # Add SHAPE reactivity constraints (Deigan method)
    # -999 entries are interpreted as "no constraint"
    fc.sc_add_SHAPE_deigan(v, float(m), float(b), 0)

    # Compute minimum free energy structure
    ss, mfe = fc.mfe()
    return ss, float(mfe)


# Ensure the SHAPE vector column stays Python objects (lists),
# not automatically converted to arrays/strings by pandas
fold_inputs["shape_vec"] = fold_inputs["shape_vec"].astype(object)

Sampling and SHAPE-Guided Folding¶

Takes a small balanced subset of sequences by sampling k examples per experiment, then compute:

  • the SHAPE-constrained minimum free energy (MFE) structure, and
  • the corresponding dot-bracket notation,

It uses the fold_with_vienna helper.
This subset is used for visualization and comparison across experimental conditions.

In [13]:
# === sample k per Experiment ===
k = 5

sample_bal = (
    fold_inputs
    .sample(frac=1, random_state=42)        # shuffle entire dataset
    .groupby("experiment", group_keys=False, observed=True)
    .head(k)                                # take first k rows per group
    .reset_index(drop=True)
    .copy()
)



# === compute dot-bracket + MFE for each sequence ===
sample_bal[["dotbracket","mfe_kcal_mol"]] = sample_bal.apply(
    lambda r: pd.Series(fold_with_vienna(r["sequence"], r["shape_vec"])),
    axis=1
)

What MFE Means in RNA Folding¶

MFE (Minimum Free Energy) refers to the predicted RNA secondary structure with the lowest free energy (ΔG).
It represents the most thermodynamically stable structure:

  • More negative ΔG → more stable / likely structure
  • Less negative ΔG → less stable / more flexible or unfolded

ViennaRNA computes the MFE structure using dynamic programming and its thermodynamic energy model.

When Using SHAPE-Guided Folding¶

With SHAPE (Selective 2′-Hydroxyl Acylation analyzed by Primer Extension) data:

  • SHAPE reactivities adjust pairing penalties to better reflect real structure
  • The reported MFE is still in kcal/mol, but now informed by both sequence and experimental reactivity
  • This produces an MFE structure that is more biologically realistic

(You may also see ensemble energy or diversity metrics, but MFE is the primary value.)

In short¶

MFE = free energy of the most stable predicted RNA structure.
With SHAPE data, the structure and its energy incorporate experimental constraints.

RNA Quality Control Metrics¶

This section computes per-sequence QC metrics to assess the reliability and behavior of SHAPE-guided folding.
It includes:

  • helpers for parsing dot-bracket pairing,
  • SHAPE vector cleaning and padding,
  • constrained folding with ViennaRNA,
  • and a qc_fold_row function that reports:
    • sequence length and SHAPE coverage,
    • capped reactivity fraction,
    • paired vs unpaired median reactivity shift,
    • DMS-specific A/C vs G/U reactivity check,
    • distance to the unconstrained MFE structure,
    • ensemble diversity from the partition function.

The QC metrics are applied row-wise to the sampled subset and merged with basic identifiers for inspection.

In [14]:
# ================================
# RNA QC helpers + per-row checks
# ================================

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import RNA  # ViennaRNA

# === helpers ===
def _pairs_mask(ss: str, L: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Return a boolean mask of length L where True marks nucleotides
    that are base-paired in a dot-bracket string `ss`.

    Notes:
      • Uses a simple stack to match '(' with ')'
      • 1-based dot-bracket indexing → convert to 0-based for mask
      • Unbalanced trailing ')' are ignored safely
    """
    m = np.zeros(L, dtype=bool)
    st = []
    for i, ch in enumerate(ss, start=1):
        if ch == '(':
            st.append(i)
        elif ch == ')':
            if not st:
                break          # unmatched ')': stop rather than crash
            i0 = st.pop()      # matching '(' position (1-based)
            m[i0 - 1] = True
            m[i - 1]  = True
    return m


def _float_list(vec, L: int) -> list[float]:
    """
    Normalize an input vector (list/array/Series) to a flat Python list
    of length L with numeric floats. Invalid or missing values are set to -999.0
    (ViennaRNA sentinel for 'no constraint').

    Behavior:
      • Truncates extra elements beyond L
      • Pads with -999.0 if shorter than L
      • Treats NaN/±inf/non-numeric as missing
    """
    v = np.array(vec, dtype=object).ravel()
    out: list[float] = []
    for x in v[:L]:
        try:
            xf = float(x)
            out.append(xf if np.isfinite(xf) else -999.0)
        except Exception:
            out.append(-999.0)
    if len(out) < L:
        out += [-999.0] * (L - len(out))
    return out


def fold_with_vienna(seq: str, vec, m: float = 1.9, b: float = -0.7) -> tuple[str, float]:
    """
    Fold an RNA sequence with ViennaRNA using SHAPE (Deigan) constraints.

    Args:
        seq: RNA/DNA sequence (any 'T' is converted to 'U')
        vec: SHAPE reactivity vector (any sequence-like); cleaned via _float_list
        m, b: Deigan parameters (slope m, intercept b)

    Returns:
        (dotbracket_structure, mfe_kcal_mol)
    """
    # Ensure RNA alphabet
    seq = str(seq).replace("T", "U")
    # Clean / pad SHAPE to sequence length
    v = _float_list(vec, len(seq))

    # Build fold compound + add SHAPE constraints; -999 are treated as missing
    fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq)
    fc.sc_add_SHAPE_deigan(v, float(m), float(b), 0)

    # Minimum Free Energy structure
    ss, mfe = fc.mfe()
    return ss, float(mfe)


def qc_fold_row(row: pd.Series, m: float = 1.9, b: float = -0.7) -> pd.Series:
    """
    Compute QC metrics for a single row containing:
      • sequence        : str
      • shape_vec       : sequence-like of SHAPE values
      • dotbracket?     : optional precomputed dot-bracket (uses it if present)
      • experiment      : optional label ("DMS" used for AC>GU check)

    Returns a Series with:
      L, coverage, frac_capped,
      delta_unpaired_minus_paired, med_AC, med_GU, dms_like_AC>GU,
      bp_distance_vs_unconstrained, ensemble_diversity
    """
    # Canonicalize inputs
    seq = str(row["sequence"]).replace("T", "U")
    L = len(seq)

    # Clean SHAPE and compute coverage stats
    v = np.array(_float_list(row["shape_vec"], L), dtype=float)
    cov = np.isfinite(v) & (v != -999.0)
    coverage = float(cov.mean())                 # fraction of positions with usable SHAPE
    frac_capped = float((v >= 10 - 1e-9).sum()) / L  # crude cap fraction at >= 10

    # Use provided constrained structure if available; otherwise fold with SHAPE
    if "dotbracket" in row and isinstance(row["dotbracket"], str):
        ss = row["dotbracket"]
    else:
        ss = fold_with_vienna(seq, v, m=m, b=b)[0]

    # === Pairing signal: median unpaired vs paired reactivity ===
    pm = _pairs_mask(ss, L)  # True where paired
    w = v.copy()
    w[~cov] = np.nan         # ignore missing when taking medians

    med_unp = float(np.nanmedian(w[~pm])) if np.any((~pm) & cov) else np.nan
    med_p   = float(np.nanmedian(w[ pm])) if np.any(( pm) & cov) else np.nan
    delta   = (med_unp - med_p) if np.isfinite(med_unp) and np.isfinite(med_p) else np.nan

    # === DMS sanity: A/C should be more reactive than G/U under DMS ===
    bases = np.frombuffer(seq.encode(), dtype="S1").astype(str)
    ac = np.isin(bases, ["A", "C"])
    med_ac = float(np.nanmedian(w[ac]))   if np.any(ac & cov)    else np.nan
    med_gu = float(np.nanmedian(w[~ac]))  if np.any((~ac) & cov) else np.nan
    dms_like = (med_ac > med_gu) if row.get("experiment") == "DMS" else np.nan

    # === Compare constrained to unconstrained MFE; ensemble diversity ===
    ss0, _ = RNA.fold_compound(seq).mfe()                 # unconstrained MFE
    bp_dist = RNA.bp_distance(ss0, ss)                    # base-pair distance between ss0 and ss

    # Partition function with constraints to get ensemble characteristics
    fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq)
    fc.sc_add_SHAPE_deigan(v.tolist(), float(m), float(b), 0)
    fc.pf()
    ensemble_div = fc.mean_bp_distance()

    return pd.Series({
        "L": L,
        "coverage": coverage,
        "frac_capped": frac_capped,
        "delta_unpaired_minus_paired": delta,
        "med_AC": med_ac,
        "med_GU": med_gu,
        "dms_like_AC>GU": dms_like,
        "bp_distance_vs_unconstrained": bp_dist,
        "ensemble_diversity": ensemble_div,
    })


# ================================
# Run QC on your selected subset
# ================================

# Make a working copy (avoid mutating the original selection)
sample_subset = sample_bal.copy()

# Ensure we have structures: fold if column is missing
if "dotbracket" not in sample_subset.columns:
    sample_subset[["dotbracket", "mfe_kcal_mol"]] = sample_subset.apply(
        lambda r: pd.Series(fold_with_vienna(r["sequence"], r["shape_vec"])),
        axis=1
    )

# Compute QC metrics row-wise
qc_sampled = sample_subset.apply(qc_fold_row, axis=1)

# Concatenate identifiers with QC metrics for a compact view
display(pd.concat(
    [
        sample_subset[["sequence_id", "experiment"]].reset_index(drop=True),
        qc_sampled.reset_index(drop=True),
    ],
    axis=1
))

What this QC table shows (RNA QC helpers + per-row checks)¶

Goal: sanity-check SHAPE data and the resulting SHAPE-guided folds.

How the code works (high level):

  • Converts T→U, cleans shape_vec to floats of length L (-999.0 = “no constraint”).
  • If dotbracket is missing, folds with ViennaRNA using Deigan parameters (m=1.9, b=-0.7).
  • Computes medians over paired vs unpaired nucleotides (from the dot-bracket) and simple QC stats.

Column glossary:

  • L — sequence length.
  • coverage — fraction of positions with usable SHAPE (finite and ≠ -999.0).
  • frac_capped — fraction of positions with very high reactivity (≥ 10); rough cap/ceiling check.
  • delta_unpaired_minus_paired — median(SHAPE at unpaired) − median(SHAPE at paired).
    Larger positive values = SHAPE agrees with pairing.
  • med_AC, med_GU — median reactivity on A/C vs G/U bases.
  • dms_like_AC>GU — for rows where experiment == "DMS", True if median(A/C) > median(G/U); else NaN.
  • bp_distance_vs_unconstrained — base-pair distance between unconstrained MFE (sequence-only) and the constrained structure used above.
  • ensemble_diversity — mean base-pair distance within the constrained ensemble (after adding SHAPE).

Notes:

  • -999.0 is ViennaRNA’s sentinel for “no SHAPE info”; those positions are ignored in medians.
  • Unbalanced ) in dot-bracket are handled defensively; unmatched closers are safely ignored.

SHAPE-Aware Folding Comparison Features¶

This section defines utilities for comparing unconstrained and SHAPE-constrained RNA folds.
It provides:

  • normalization of SHAPE vectors,
  • unconstrained (NC) and SHAPE-constrained (SC) folding functions,
  • base-pairing masks from dot-bracket strings,
  • and add_compare_features, which computes:
    • constrained vs unconstrained MFE,
    • base-pair distance,
    • ensemble diversity (NC and SC),
    • ΔED and ΔMFE,
    • and the separation between unpaired/paired SHAPE signals.

The resulting features summarize how SHAPE data influences the predicted structure for each sequence.

In [16]:
# ================================
# SHAPE-aware folding & comparison helpers (ViennaRNA)
# ================================

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import RNA  # ViennaRNA

def _float_list(vec, L):
    """
    Normalize a SHAPE vector to a Python list[float] of length L.

    Rules:
      - Cast to float where possible.
      - Replace invalid / None / NaN / ±inf with -999.0 (ViennaRNA sentinel = "no constraint").
      - Truncate to L if longer; pad with -999.0 if shorter.
    """
    v = np.array(vec, dtype=object).ravel()
    out = []
    for x in v[:L]:
        try:
            xf = float(x)
            out.append(xf if np.isfinite(xf) else -999.0)
        except Exception:
            out.append(-999.0)
    if len(out) < L:
        out += [-999.0] * (L - len(out))
    return out


def fold_nc(seq):
    """
    Unconstrained MFE folding (sequence only).
    Returns: (dot_bracket, mfe_kcal_mol)
    """
    seq = str(seq).replace("T", "U")
    fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq)
    ss, mfe = fc.mfe()
    return ss, float(mfe)


def fold_sc(seq, vec, m=1.9, b=-0.7):
    """
    SHAPE-constrained MFE folding using Deigan pseudo-energies.
    Args:
        seq : RNA/DNA (T→U converted)
        vec : SHAPE reactivity vector (any sequence-like)
        m,b : Deigan parameters (slope, intercept)
    Returns:
        (dot_bracket, mfe_kcal_mol, cleaned_shape_list)
    """
    seq = str(seq).replace("T", "U")
    v = _float_list(vec, len(seq))
    fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq)
    # -999 values are interpreted as "no constraint"
    fc.sc_add_SHAPE_deigan(v, float(m), float(b), 0)
    ss, mfe = fc.mfe()
    return ss, float(mfe), v


def paired_mask(ss):
    """
    Build a boolean mask (len = len(ss)) where True marks paired positions
    in a dot-bracket string. Uses a stack to match '(' with ')'.
    """
    m = np.zeros(len(ss), dtype=bool)
    st = []
    for i, ch in enumerate(ss):
        if ch == '(':
            st.append(i)
        elif ch == ')' and st:
            j = i
            i0 = st.pop()
            m[i0] = True
            m[j]  = True
    return m


def add_compare_features(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    For each row with columns:
        sequence, shape_vec, (optional) dotbracket, (optional) mfe_kcal_mol
    compute and add:
        - dotbracket_nc, mfe_nc                (unconstrained fold)
        - bp_distance                          (unconstrained vs constrained structure)
        - ED_nc, ED_sc, dED                    (ensemble diversity)
        - dMFE                                 (mfe_sc - mfe_nc; note sc includes pseudo-energies)
        - signal_sep                           (median_unpaired - median_paired, on constrained ss)

    Returns a copy of df with added columns; does not mutate input.
    """
    out = df.copy()

    # Ensure constrained folding results exist (compute if missing)
    if not {"dotbracket", "mfe_kcal_mol"}.issubset(out.columns):
        out[["dotbracket", "mfe_kcal_mol"]] = out.apply(
            lambda r: pd.Series(fold_sc(r["sequence"], r["shape_vec"])[:2]),
            axis=1
        )

    # Unconstrained folding (sequence-only baseline)
    out[["dotbracket_nc", "mfe_nc"]] = out.apply(
        lambda r: pd.Series(fold_nc(r["sequence"])),
        axis=1
    )

    # Base-pair distance between unconstrained and constrained structures
    out["bp_distance"] = out.apply(
        lambda r: RNA.bp_distance(r["dotbracket_nc"], r["dotbracket"]),
        axis=1
    )

    # Ensemble diversity helpers (mean base-pair distance over ensemble)
    def _ed_nc(seq: str) -> float:
        fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq.replace("T", "U"))
        fc.pf()
        return fc.mean_bp_distance()

    def _ed_sc(seq: str, vec) -> float:
        s = seq.replace("T", "U")
        v = _float_list(vec, len(s))
        fc = RNA.fold_compound(s)
        fc.sc_add_SHAPE_deigan(v, 1.9, -0.7, 0)
        fc.pf()
        return fc.mean_bp_distance()

    out["ED_nc"] = out["sequence"].apply(_ed_nc)
    out["ED_sc"] = out.apply(lambda r: _ed_sc(r["sequence"], r["shape_vec"]), axis=1)
    out["dED"]   = out["ED_sc"] - out["ED_nc"]

    # ΔMFE (sc includes SHAPE pseudo-energies; not directly comparable to pure thermodynamics)
    out["dMFE"] = out["mfe_kcal_mol"] - out["mfe_nc"]

    # Signal separation on constrained structure: median(unpaired) - median(paired)
    def _sep(r) -> float:
        s = r["sequence"].replace("T", "U")
        v = np.array(_float_list(r["shape_vec"], len(s)), dtype=float)
        cov = np.isfinite(v) & (v != -999.0)      # positions with usable SHAPE
        pm  = paired_mask(r["dotbracket"])        # True for paired nucs
        unp = (~pm) & cov
        pai = pm & cov
        med_unp = np.nan if not np.any(unp) else float(np.nanmedian(v[unp]))
        med_p   = np.nan if not np.any(pai) else float(np.nanmedian(v[pai]))
        return np.nan if (np.isnan(med_unp) or np.isnan(med_p)) else (med_unp - med_p)

    out["signal_sep"] = out.apply(_sep, axis=1)

    return out
#compute
features_5 = add_compare_features(sample_bal.copy())

What this comparison/features table shows (SHAPE-aware folding & comparison)¶

Goal: quantify how SHAPE constraints change folding and the ensemble, relative to the sequence-only baseline.

How the code works (high level):

  • Ensures a constrained fold exists (dotbracket, mfe_kcal_mol); computes it if missing using Deigan (m=1.9, b=-0.7).
  • Always computes the unconstrained fold (dotbracket_nc, mfe_nc).
  • Compares structures, MFEs, and ensemble diversities with and without SHAPE.

Column glossary:

  • mfe_nc — MFE (kcal/mol) for the unconstrained (sequence-only) fold.
  • mfe_kcal_mol — MFE for the constrained (SHAPE-guided) fold.
  • dMFE — mfe_kcal_mol − mfe_nc.
    Caution: constrained MFE includes pseudo-energies from SHAPE; it’s not directly comparable to pure thermodynamics, so dMFE is a feature, not a physical ΔG difference.
  • bp_distance — base-pair distance between dotbracket_nc (unconstrained) and dotbracket (constrained).
  • ED_nc, ED_sc — ensemble diversity (mean base-pair distance) without vs with SHAPE.
    ED_sc is computed after applying Deigan constraints; ED_nc from the sequence-only partition function.
  • dED — ED_sc − ED_nc; how constraints sharpen (negative) or broaden (positive) the ensemble.
  • signal_sep — median(SHAPE at unpaired) − median(SHAPE at paired) evaluated on the constrained structure (same concept as the QC table’s delta_unpaired_minus_paired).

Notes:

  • The helper always converts T→U and cleans shape_vec to length L with -999.0 for missing values.
  • bp_distance is a structural change metric: higher values = bigger topology difference between unconstrained and constrained folds.

SHAPE Parameter Sweep (Deigan m, b)¶

This block evaluates how different SHAPE pseudo-energy parameters (slope m, intercept b) affect RNA folding outcomes.
For each parameter pair, we compute:

  • unconstrained vs constrained structures,
  • base-pair distance (structure change),
  • ΔMFE between modes,
  • ensemble diversity (NC and SC),
  • and summary statistics across the sampled sequences.

The result is a compact comparison table showing how SHAPE weighting influences fold stability and structural deviation.

In [17]:
# === Helper: Unconstrained folding (sequence-only) ===
def fold_nc(seq):
    seq = str(seq).replace("T","U")     # ensure RNA alphabet
    fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq)        # build folding object
    return fc.mfe()                    # return (structure, MFE)


# === Helper: SHAPE-constrained folding (Deigan) ===
def fold_sc(seq, vec, m, b):
    seq = str(seq).replace("T","U")    # T→U
    # Clean SHAPE vector: cast to float, invalid → -999 sentinel
    v = np.array(vec, dtype=object)
    v = [float(x) if np.isfinite(float(x)) else -999.0 for x in v]

    fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq)
    # Add Deigan pseudo-energy constraints
    #   m = slope, b = intercept
    #   -999 means "ignore this position"
    fc.sc_add_SHAPE_deigan(v, float(m), float(b), 0)

    # Return:
    #   (structure, MFE) and the fc object (for reuse in PF/ED calculation)
    return fc.mfe(), (fc, v)


# === Helper: ensemble diversity on an existing fold_compound ===
def mean_bp_distance(fc):
    fc.pf()                          # compute partition function (full ensemble)
    return fc.mean_bp_distance()     # mean base-pair distance = "ensemble diversity"


# ============ Dataset Setup ============
sub = sample_bal.copy()  # reuse same subset used previously

# Compute unconstrained fold baseline once for each sequence
sub[["ss_nc","mfe_nc"]] = sub.apply(
    lambda r: pd.Series(fold_nc(r["sequence"])), axis=1
)


# ============ Parameter grid to test ============
# Sweep different Deigan (m, b) settings
grid = [
    (1.2, -0.5),   # mild SHAPE effect
    (1.9, -0.7),   # standard default
    (2.5, -0.7),   # stronger slope effect
    (3.0, -0.8),   # very strong penalty/bonus
]


rows = []  # store summary results per (m, b)

for m, b in grid:
    tmp = sub.copy()

    # Compute constrained folding for each sequence
    tmp[["ss_sc","mfe_sc","_fc"]] = tmp.apply(
        lambda r: pd.Series(
            (
                # fold once for structure + MFE
                *fold_sc(r["sequence"], r["shape_vec"], m, b)[0],
                # store fold_compound for partition function reuse
                fold_sc(r["sequence"], r["shape_vec"], m, b)[1][0]
            )
        ),
        axis=1
    )

    # Structural distance: unconstrained vs constrained
    tmp["bp_dist"] = tmp.apply(
        lambda r: RNA.bp_distance(r["ss_nc"], r["ss_sc"]), axis=1
    )

    # ΔMFE (note: sc includes pseudo-energies; not a thermodynamic ΔG)
    tmp["dMFE"] = tmp["mfe_sc"] - tmp["mfe_nc"]

    # Unconstrained ensemble diversity
    tmp["ED_nc"] = tmp["sequence"].apply(
        lambda s: (
            lambda fc: (fc.pf(), fc.mean_bp_distance())
        )(RNA.fold_compound(s.replace("T","U")))[1]
    )

    # Constrained ensemble diversity
    tmp["ED_sc"] = tmp["_fc"].apply(mean_bp_distance)

    # ΔED
    tmp["dED"] = tmp["ED_sc"] - tmp["ED_nc"]

    # Add summary statistics for this (m, b) setting
    rows.append({
        "m": m, "b": b,
        "median_bp_dist": float(np.median(tmp["bp_dist"])),
        "mean_bp_distance": float(np.mean(tmp["bp_dist"])),
        "median_dMFE": float(np.median(tmp["dMFE"])),
        "mean_dMFE": float(np.mean(tmp["dMFE"])),
        "median_dED": float(np.median(tmp["dED"])),
        "mean_dED": float(np.mean(tmp["dED"])),
    })


# Final parameter-sweep summary table
pd.DataFrame(rows)

What this Deigan-parameter sweep table shows¶

Goal: explore how different Deigan SHAPE parameters (slope m, intercept b) affect structures, energies, and ensembles across your subset.

How the code works (high level):

  • Defines helpers:
    • fold_nc(seq) → unconstrained MFE (ss_nc, mfe_nc).
    • fold_sc(seq, vec, m, b) → SHAPE-constrained MFE (ss_sc, mfe_sc) and returns the fold compound fc so we can reuse it for partition function & ensemble metrics.
    • mean_bp_distance(fc) → runs pf() on the given fc and returns ensemble diversity (mean base-pair distance).
  • Builds a small grid of (m, b) values and, for each pair, folds every sequence with SHAPE constraints, compares to the unconstrained baseline, and aggregates summary stats.

Per-grid metrics (columns):

  • m, b — Deigan parameters used for that sweep point.
  • median_bp_dist, mean_bp_dist — base-pair distance (unconstrained vs constrained) summarized across sequences.
    Higher ⇒ the constrained structure differs more from the sequence-only fold.
  • median_dMFE, mean_dMFE — mfe_sc − mfe_nc summarized.
    Caution: mfe_sc includes pseudo-energies from SHAPE, so dMFE is a feature for comparison, not a thermodynamic ΔG.
  • median_dED, mean_dED — change in ensemble diversity ED_sc − ED_nc summarized.
    Negative ⇒ constraints sharpen the ensemble (more focused); positive ⇒ broader ensemble.

Implementation notes:

  • All sequences are normalized to RNA (T→U), and SHAPE vectors are cast to float with invalids → -999.0 (ViennaRNA’s “no constraint” sentinel).
  • The constrained fold returns fc so we can reuse the same setup for pf() when computing ED_sc.
  • ED_nc is computed from a fresh unconstrained fold_compound per sequence.
  • Interpretation tip: as m increases (steeper penalty/bonus from SHAPE), you generally expect bp_dist ↑ and often ED_sc ↓ (tighter ensembles), but real data can vary.

The following code uses the classical/default ViennaRNA setup and also non-constrained and exagerated constraint to show the impact on 2-d folding¶

  • Based on Deigan et al., PNAS 2009
  • Slope = 1.8, Intercept = –0.6
  • This is what ViennaRNA uses if you don’t specify otherwise (--shapeMethod D).

RNA Structure Visualization¶

This section defines reusable tools for rendering RNA secondary structures with forgi and ViennaRNA.
It includes:

  • SHAPE vector cleaning and robust normalization,
  • a white→red colormap for reactivity values,
  • text and annotation cleanup tailored for forgi,
  • unconstrained and SHAPE-constrained folding helpers,
  • and a unified render_rna_plot function that produces dark-themed, publication-ready diagrams.

Computes unconstrained, constrained, and strongly constrained folds for each sampled sequence and exports the corresponding structure images for visual comparison.

In [26]:
# =========================
# Shared helpers + defaults
# =========================

# plt.style.use("dark_background")  # set once
dark_col = "#17191a"

BASES = {"A", "C", "G", "U", "T"}
LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"[sihmSIHM]\d+")  # precompile once

def to_float_list(vec):
    """Cast vec to floats; invalid -> -999.0 (ViennaRNA sentinel)."""
    v = np.asarray(vec, dtype=object).ravel()
    out = np.empty(v.size, dtype=float)
    for i, x in enumerate(v):
        try:
            fx = float(x)
            out[i] = fx if np.isfinite(fx) else -999.0
        except Exception:
            out[i] = -999.0
    return out.tolist()

def robust_percentile_norm(df, col="shape_vec", low=5, high=95):
    """Global vmin/vmax based on robust percentiles over all rows (skipping -999 and NaN)."""
    arrays = []
    for vec in df[col].values:
        a = np.asarray(vec, dtype=float)
        if a.ndim == 0:
            continue
        a = a[(a != -999) & np.isfinite(a)]
        if a.size:
            arrays.append(a)
    if arrays:
        flat = np.concatenate(arrays)
        vmin, vmax = np.percentile(flat, [low, high])
        if not np.isfinite(vmin) or not np.isfinite(vmax) or vmax <= vmin:
            vmin = float(np.nanmin(flat))
            vmax = float(np.nanmax(flat))
            if not np.isfinite(vmin) or not np.isfinite(vmax) or vmax <= vmin:
                vmin, vmax = 0.0, 1.0
    else:
        vmin, vmax = 0.0, 1.0
    if vmax <= vmin:
        center, span = float(vmin), 1e-3
        vmin, vmax = center - span/2, center + span/2
    return mcolors.Normalize(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, clip=True), (vmin, vmax)

def white_to_red_cmap():
    return mcolors.LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("white_to_red", ["#ffffff", "#ff0000"])


def clean_axes_texts(ax):
    base_texts, number_texts = [], []

    for p in list(ax.patches):
        if isinstance(p, (matplotlib.patches.Circle, matplotlib.patches.FancyArrowPatch)):
            p.remove()

    for t in list(ax.texts):
        s = (t.get_text() or "").strip()

        # Turn Annotations into simple Text before we style them
        if isinstance(t, Annotation):
            # remove arrow artist if present
            ap = getattr(t, "arrow_patch", None)
            if ap is not None:
                try: ap.remove()
                except Exception: pass
            # re-create as Text at the same position
            x, y = t.xy if hasattr(t, "xy") else t.get_position()
            new_t = ax.text(
                x, y, s,
                fontsize=t.get_fontsize(),
                ha=t.get_ha(), va=t.get_va(),
                rotation=t.get_rotation(),
                color=t.get_color()
            )
            t.remove()
            t = new_t  # continue with plain Text

        if s.upper() in BASES:
            base_texts.append(t)
        elif s.isdigit():
            number_texts.append(t)
        elif LABEL_RE.fullmatch(s):
            t.remove()
        else:
            t.remove()
    return base_texts, number_texts


def recolor_bases(base_texts, shape_vec, norm, cmap, missing_rgba=(1,1,1,0.35), fontsize=8):
    L = min(len(base_texts), len(shape_vec))
    # Vectorized mask + normalization to cut Python loop work
    sv = np.asarray(shape_vec, dtype=float)
    valid = np.isfinite(sv) & (sv != -999)
    # Clip only valid values for mapping
    clipped = np.empty(L, dtype=float)
    clipped[:] = np.nan
    vals = np.clip(sv[:L], norm.vmin, norm.vmax, out=clipped[:L], where=np.isfinite(sv[:L]))
    # Assign colors
    for i in range(L):
        if i < sv.size and valid[i]:
            color = cmap(norm(vals[i]))
        else:
            color = missing_rgba
        bt = base_texts[i]
        bt.set_color(color)
        bt.set_fontweight("bold")
        bt.set_fontsize(fontsize)

def add_colorbar(ax, norm, cmap, label="SHAPE reactivity", ticksize=8):
    sm = matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=cmap)
    sm.set_array([])
    cbar = ax.figure.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)
    cbar.set_label(label)
    cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=ticksize)

# =========================
# Folding helpers (reused)
# =========================
def fold_unconstrained(seq):
    seq = str(seq).replace("T", "U")
    fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq)
    return fc.mfe()  # (dotbracket, mfe)

def fold_deigan(seq, vec, m=1.9, b=-0.7):
    """SHAPE-constrained fold with Deigan; returns (dotbracket, mfe)."""
    seq = str(seq).replace("T", "U")
    v = to_float_list(vec)
    if len(v) != len(seq):
        raise ValueError(f"shape_vec length {len(v)} != sequence length {len(seq)}")
    fc = RNA.fold_compound(seq)
    fc.sc_add_SHAPE_deigan(v, float(m), float(b), 0)
    ss, mfe = fc.mfe()
    return ss, float(mfe)

# =========================================
# One unified plotter used by all pipelines
# =========================================
def render_rna_plot(dotbracket, seq, shape_vec, title, outpath, cmap, norm):
    """
    Draw using forgi, recolor bases by SHAPE (if shape_vec provided), add colorbar, save.
    If shape_vec is None, bases are white (unconstrained view).
    """
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message="invalid value", module="forgi.visual.mplotlib")

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))

        # ▲ Apply dark theme on figure and axes
        fig.patch.set_facecolor(dark_col)
        ax.set_facecolor(dark_col)

        # ▲ Ensure default text is white
        for spine in ax.spines.values():
            spine.set_color("white")

        bg = fgb.BulgeGraph.from_dotbracket(dotbracket, seq)
        fvm.plot_rna(
            bg,
            lighten=0.25,
            text_kwargs={"fontsize": 8, "color": "white"},   # ▲ ensure white base text by default
            backbone_kwargs={"linewidth": 2, "alpha": 0.25, "color": "white"},   # ▲ white-ish backbone
            basepair_kwargs={"linewidth": 2, "alpha": 0.35, "color": "white"},   # ▲ white-ish pair lines
        )

        # Clean/collect text objects
        base_texts, number_texts = clean_axes_texts(ax)

        # Shift numbering labels
        xmin, xmax = ax.get_xlim()
        ymin, ymax = ax.get_ylim()
        xscale = (xmax - xmin) * 0.03
        yscale = (ymax - ymin) * 0.03

        for nt in number_texts:
            x, y = nt.get_position()
            nt.set_position((x + xscale, y + yscale))
            nt.set_fontsize(7)
            nt.set_color("lightgray")   # ▲ move away from dark

        # Constrained vs unconstrained coloring logic
        if shape_vec is None:
            # ▲ All bases white
            for t in base_texts:
                t.set_color("white")
                t.set_fontweight("bold")
                t.set_fontsize(8)
        else:
            recolor_bases(
                base_texts,
                np.asarray(shape_vec, dtype=float),
                norm,
                cmap,
                missing_rgba=(1, 1, 1, 0.35),
                fontsize=8
            )

        # ▲ Colorbar: white labels
        sm = matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=cmap)
        sm.set_array([])
        cbar = ax.figure.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)
        cbar.set_label("SHAPE reactivity", color="white")
        cbar.ax.yaxis.set_tick_params(color="white")
        plt.setp(plt.getp(cbar.ax.axes, 'yticklabels'), color='white')

        # ▲ Title white
        ax.set_title(title, color="white")

        try:
            plt.tight_layout()
        except:
            fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.10, right=0.97, top=0.90, bottom=0.12)

        outpath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        fig.savefig(outpath, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor=dark_col)
        plt.close(fig)

# =========================
# How to use the utilities
# =========================

# 1) Build a single global norm + cmap for the WHOLE subset (skip -999)
norm, (vmin, vmax) = robust_percentile_norm(sample_bal, col="shape_vec")
cmap = white_to_red_cmap()

# 2) Compute folds ONCE (avoid double calls inside apply)
#    Unconstrained
if not {"dotbracket_nc", "mfe_nc"}.issubset(sample_bal.columns):
    sample_bal[["dotbracket_nc", "mfe_nc"]] = sample_bal.apply(
        lambda r: pd.Series(fold_unconstrained(r["sequence"])),
        axis=1
    )

#    Constrained (default)
if not {"dotbracket_sc", "mfe_kcal_mol_sc"}.issubset(sample_bal.columns):
    sample_bal[["dotbracket_sc", "mfe_kcal_mol_sc"]] = sample_bal.apply(
        lambda r: pd.Series(fold_deigan(r["sequence"], r["shape_vec"], m=1.9, b=-0.7)),
        axis=1
    )

#    Strong-constrained (optional; separate columns to compare)
if not {"dotbracket_strong", "mfe_kcal_mol_strong"}.issubset(sample_bal.columns):
    sample_bal[["dotbracket_strong", "mfe_kcal_mol_strong"]] = sample_bal.apply(
        lambda r: pd.Series(fold_deigan(r["sequence"], r["shape_vec"], m=2.8, b=0.0)),
        axis=1
    )

# 3) Plot in three passes with a single renderer (no repeated boilerplate)
out_nc  = OUT_ROOT / "rna_kaggle_skeleton/outputs/unconstrained"
out_sc  = OUT_ROOT / "rna_kaggle_skeleton/outputs/constrained"
out_str = OUT_ROOT / "rna_kaggle_skeleton/outputs/strong_constrained"

# Use itertuples for speed; avoid .iterrows overhead
for r in sample_bal.itertuples(index=True):
    # Unconstrained
    title_nc = f"{getattr(r, 'sequence_id', r.Index)} | {getattr(r, 'experiment', 'NA')} | MFE={r.mfe_nc:.2f} (no SHAPE)"
    render_rna_plot(
        dotbracket=r.dotbracket_nc,
        seq=r.sequence,
        shape_vec=None,                   # no coloring for unconstrained
        title=title_nc,
        outpath=out_nc / f"{getattr(r, 'sequence_id', r.Index)}_folding_nc.png",
        cmap=cmap, norm=norm
    )

    # Constrained (default)
    title_sc = f"{getattr(r, 'sequence_id', r.Index)} | {getattr(r, 'experiment', 'NA')} | MFE={r.mfe_kcal_mol_sc:.2f}"
    render_rna_plot(
        dotbracket=r.dotbracket_sc,
        seq=r.sequence,
        shape_vec=getattr(r, "shape_vec"),
        title=title_sc,
        outpath=out_sc / f"{getattr(r, 'sequence_id', r.Index)}_folding_sc.png",
        cmap=cmap, norm=norm
    )

    # Strong constrained
    title_str = f"{getattr(r, 'sequence_id', r.Index)} | {getattr(r, 'experiment', 'NA')} | MFE={r.mfe_kcal_mol_strong:.2f} (strong)"
    render_rna_plot(
        dotbracket=r.dotbracket_strong,
        seq=r.sequence,
        shape_vec=getattr(r, "shape_vec"),
        title=title_str,
        outpath=out_str / f"{getattr(r, 'sequence_id', r.Index)}_folding_strong.png",
        cmap=cmap, norm=norm
    )

SHAPE Reactivity Color Scale Interpretation¶

Color Meaning Structural Interpretation SHAPE Reactivity
White Low flexibility Likely base-paired / structured region Low
Light Red / Pink Moderate flexibility Partially flexible / transient structure Medium
Bright Red High flexibility Likely unpaired / loop / bulge / single-stranded High
Faded White / Transparent Missing / invalid value (-999) No SHAPE information N/A

Grid Display of Generated RNA Structure Images¶

This section provides a simple helper (show_grid) to preview the exported RNA structure images for each folding mode.
It loads the first few PNGs from each output directory and displays them in a 2×2 dark-themed grid, allowing quick visual comparison of:

  • unconstrained folds,
  • SHAPE-constrained folds,
  • and strong-constraint folds.

This offers a fast overview of how constraints affect predicted RNA structure.

In [29]:
def show_grid(pattern, title):
    files = glob.glob(pattern)[:6]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 8))
    fig.suptitle(title, color="white", fontsize=16)

    for ax, f in zip(axes.flatten(), files):
        ax.imshow(Image.open(f))
        #ax.set_title(f.split("/")[-1], color="white")
        ax.axis("off")
        ax.set_facecolor(dark_col)  # ensure no bright borders

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


show_grid("rna_kaggle_skeleton/outputs/constrained/*.png",       "Folding with constrained outputs")
show_grid("rna_kaggle_skeleton/outputs/strong_constrained/*.png","Folding with strong constrained outputs")
show_grid("rna_kaggle_skeleton/outputs/unconstrained/*.png",     "Folding with unconstrained outputs")
